candidates.source_title: Adult gaming centre plan for Subway after nail bar bid is pulled - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Middleton could have two adult gaming arcades within feet of each other if new plans get the green light. JR Planning Consultants has applied to Rochdale Council to turn the Subway store at 16 Middleton Gardens into an adult gaming centre. It follows an application it submitted in July to turn the premises into a nail bar. That application has since been withdrawn. In the latest application, JR Planning said the Planning Inspectorate appeal which allowed Jeffries Casino to occupy the former Virgin Money premises at 20 Middleton Gardens had set a precedent for the change of use in a retail area. It said: “The Inspector found that the proposed adult gaming centre was likely to generate greater footfall over a typical day than many potential Class E uses. “The Inspector also found that the use would provide opportunities for linked trips to shops, pubs and other town centre businesses and make a modest contribution to the functioning of the centre. “It was concluded that the adult gaming centre would form part of a suitable mix of uses complementary to the retail role of Middleton town centre. Therefore, the vitality and viability of the centre would not be undermined. “The Inspector also considered the potential concentration of adult gaming centres. It was concluded that the establishment of an additional non-retail unit would not be materially harmful to the vitality and viability of the town centre.

candidates.source_title: After decades of decay, Rochdale's Chernobyl is finally getting cleaned up - Manchester Evening News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The derelict asbestos factory in Rochdale will soon be cleaned up, which is a major milestone in the path towards redevelopment, according to the landowners. Decaying, dangerous and eerie are all words that would accurately describe the former Turner Brothers factory in the Spotland area of Rochdale . It used to be the world’s largest asbestos manufacturer and once employed thousands in the town, but it has sat empty for decades. It is off-limits to the public and only foolhardy ‘urban explorers’ dare trespass onto the site nicknamed ‘Rochdale’s Chernobyl’. Locally, there has been a long held ambition to see the site bulldozed and brought back into use for the good of the community. Creating a park, to seamlessly blend with the surrounding greenery, is the popular option for locals. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter But the numerous redevelopment schemes have all included housing as well as various ideas for public open spaces. After a number of failed attempts at redevelopment, Spodden Park Ltd are the latest to try their hand at bringing the 75-acre site back into use. Although their future vision for the area off Spod Road has not been revealed, it is understood there is an ambition to build housing and create a park in some capacity. No details have been confirmed by the landowner, but they have outlined that the number of houses planned would be far fewer than the 650 previously touted in the 2000s. Spodden Park Limited took control of the site from ESG Trading Limited in 2024, but they’ve been slow to table their vision. They’ve previously explained that this is because they want to do things as safely as possible. This is understandable considering the carcinogenic nature of the asbestos previously produced on site. Their latest announcement has been to sign a contractor to deliver the clean up of the site - remediation. It is understood that once this is completed, the former asbestos production site will actually become viable for development When the Manchester Evening News toured the site last year , the foliage at head height was hard to ignore, as was the level of deterioration of the old factory buildings themselves. It is unknown what the remediation work will actually entail, but some level of demolition work could be included as part of it. candidates.source_title: New governor will help ease pressure on gas network - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: New equipment could be installed to help meet demand for gas in an area of Middleton. MacMarshalls Rural Chartered Surveyors & Planning Consultants has applied on behalf of Cadent Gas Ltd to Rochdale Council to install a new gas governor, kiosk and fencing next to 56 Bonscale Crescent in Middleton. The kiosk is earmarked for a corner of the open space — which also includes a children’s play area — closest to the road and against the boundary with 56 Bonscale Crescent. The application follows a previous plan to install the kiosk beside 54 Bonscale Crescent. That application was withdrawn. In planning documents submitted to the council, MacMarshalls said: “The works are driven by current pressure on the existing gas network, which means a new gas governor is required to cope with demand for gas in the local area. “Gas governors are essential to the safe distribution of gas and are designed to control gas pressure in the locality, reducing pressure from high to low in order to feed local residents and businesses. “Gas usage in the area is high from both commercial and residential end users, and the local area is therefore reliant on the gas governor, hence the requirement to install a new kiosk in this area. “The kiosk itself would not, as a standalone operation, require planning permission, as it would fall within the permitted parameters. The proposed kiosk is 26.8 cubic metres, with permitted development allowing for the installation of a structure for housing apparatus not exceeding 29 cubic metres.

candidates.source_title: Rochdale strike late to beat Swindon soon after visitors reduced to 10 men - prestwichandwhitefieldguide.co.uk
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Cian Hayes headed a late winner as Rochdale capitalised on Swindon having a man sent off to secure a 1-0 victory and increase the pressure on Ian Holloway. Under-fire Robins’ boss Holloway branded himself a “dead man walking” in a viral pre-match interview but his side looked to have done enough to secure a welcome point at the Crown Oil Arena. But Kaelan Majekodunmi was sent off for a second bookable offence in the 85th minute and Rochdale struck three minutes later to snatch the points as Hayes glanced home Aden Flint’s knock-on. Neither goalkeeper had been seriously tested in the opening half, though it took Flint’s timely intervention to prevent Anthony Munda’s low drive from troubling Nils Ramming in the Rochdale goal. After the interval, Antwoine Hackford was denied by Ramming while Rochdale frontman Dajaune Brown missed a golden opportunity in the 66th minute when he got his feet in a tangle and failed to convert Glenn Middleton’s inviting delivery. Brown saw a volleyed effort pushed over the bar by Connor Ripley, who later saved brilliantly from Charlie Tasker before Hayes delivered the decisive blow.

candidates.source_title: 'Sickening' - Holloway frustrated as Swindon get no luck in defeat at Rochdale - swindonadvertiser.co.uk
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Ian Holloway said that it was "sickening" for Swindon Town to lose 1-0 at Rochdale after what he felt was their best away performance. Swindon were without half of their squad at Rochdale, but turned in a strong display, and would have been disappointed not to be ahead after 70 minutes as they failed to make a few big chances count. But without reinforcements on the bench, the hosts came on strong, and two yellow cards for Kaelan Majekodunmi proved too much to contend with, and Cian Hayes headed in the winner with two minutes to play. Swindon had just 15 players to pick from for the game, and it could have been less than that after Joseph Hungbo had a niggle in his knee in training before travelling. That meant that even the substitutes were not fully fit, making it an even tougher task for Swindon to end their tough run away from home, where they are still yet to win or score. Holloway said that there was so much to like about what Swindon did, but they just let themselves down at the end. He said: "That is sickening for everybody. "When you put your lives on the line like that lads did today, and there were some fantastic performances, it is tough to take.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: This week's faith news from the Rochdale area Last Sunday we had our joint Harvest Festival at St Barnabas Church taken by Revd Roger Hill and this week we will celebrate Holy Communion officiated by Revd Ian Stamp. The service will be followed by tea, coffee and biscuits giving us all a time to chat and get to know each other and also any visitors who are usually among us. We used to perform two productions each year which were very successful and have now found that we need some space so have been selling most of the costumes since we have ended the theatre group. The reason, as we have said here before, is due to the fact that the costs of producing shows have for us become rather excessive. That being said, we feel sad for the children who thoroughly enjoyed being connected with the production and the confidence that they found. Due to this decision, we still have many boxes of unsold costumes. We have been exceptionally lucky because when we decided to dispose of some costumes we found that societies throughout the world were interested in buying some. There are also some backcloths available too. We have sold some to societies in Germany, Italy, Norway and America, not bad for a little church in Littleborough. Indeed, our first Joseph and first Wizard of Oz costumes were sold to professional theatre companies in England. But our The King and I costumes have been to an American company. That having been said, we have successfully sold some on eBay. However, we still have lots of costumes to sell including some military items. candidates.source_title: Warsaw Uprising exhibition launched at Bury’s Fusilier Museum
candidates.source_body_excerpt: An exhibition about the Warsaw Uprising of 1944 was launched at the Fusilier Museum in Bury on Thursday evening, October 1. Warsaw Calling: Uprising 1944 explores the Polish underground resistance’s uprising against Nazi occupation, which began on August 1, 1944. Resistance fighters and civilians fought for the liberation of Warsaw for 63 days. The exhibition uses personal stories, archival material and images to tell the stories of those who lived through the uprising. It was curated by the Polish Underground Movement Study Trust in partnership with Polonia Northern England. A complementary display, Northern Heroines, tells the stories of three women connected to the Polish community in the North of England. It was produced by Polonia Northern England. Warsaw Calling: Uprising 1944 runs until February 27, 2027. Entry is included in museum admission. The museum is on Moss Street, Bury, BL9 0DF. Admission costs £4.95 for adults, £3.95 for concessions, £2.95 for children and £9.95 for families. Tickets include an annual pass allowing repeat visits for 12 months.

candidates.source_title: Details of new Scout Moor wind farm revealed
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A new wind farm planned for moorland between Rochdale and Bury has reduced in size, but it’s still not good enough for opposing campaigners. The Say NO to Scout Moor 2 group has objected to Cubico Sustainable Investments plan for ‘Scout Moor 2’ ever since they were first mooted back in 2024. Campaigners fear the turbines – up to 180m including blade tip height – would be larger than Blackpool Tower and dominate the skyline. The latest changes from Cubico have seen the scheme dropped from 17 wind turbines to 12. This reduction means that the proposed windfarm would only have the potential to power 84,552 homes annually, rather than 100,000 previously touted. There is already a wind farm in operation on Scout Moor. But according to planning documents, the farm would be run separately and have a life span of around 40 years. Planning papers also highlight the need for underground cables connected to an on-site substation, which will later be hooked up to a supply point in Rossendale to deliver electricity to the National Grid. The clean energy generation from the turbines is said to recover the fossil fuel costs to build the new wind farm in 18 months. They’ve also said the excavation of peat, a pivotal carbon dioxide capture source, will be reduced by 28 per cent. Cubico has promised a peat restoration project so the extracted peat will not be lost entirely. This is something objectors don’t believe is realistic. Cubico also said they are avoiding placing turbines that dominate local viewpoints. But these statements have also been challenged by local campaigners.
candidates.source_summary: A new wind farm planned for moorland between Rochdale and Bury has reduced in size, but it’s still not good enough for opposing campaigners.

candidates.source_title: Could the Turner Brothers factory finally be getting cleared up
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The derelict asbestos factory in Rochdale will soon be cleaned up, which is a major milestone in the path towards redevelopment, according to the landowners. Decaying, dangerous and eerie are all words that would accurately describe the former Turner Brothers factory in the Spotland area of Rochdale. It used to be the world’s largest asbestos manufacturer and once employed thousands in the town, but it has sat empty for decades. It is off-limits to the public and only foolhardy ‘urban explorers’ dare trespass onto the site nicknamed ‘Rochdale’s Chernobyl’. Locally, there has been a long held ambition to see the site bulldozed and brought back into use for the good of the community. Creating a park, to seamlessly blend with the surrounding greenery, is the popular option for locals. But the numerous redevelopment schemes have all included housing as well as various ideas for public open spaces. After a number of failed attempts at redevelopment, Spodden Park Ltd are the latest to try their hand at bringing the 75-acre site back into use. Although their future vision for the area off Spod Road has not been revealed, it is understood there is an ambition to build housing and create a park in some capacity. No details have been confirmed by the landowner, but they have outlined that the number of houses planned would be far fewer than the 650 previously touted in the 2000s. Spodden Park Limited took control of the site from ESG Trading Limited in 2024, but they’ve been slow to table their vision. They’ve previously explained that this is because they want to do things as safely as possible. This is understandable considering the carcinogenic nature of the asbestos previously produced on site. Their latest announcement has been to sign a contractor to deliver the clean up of the site – remediation. It is understood that once this is completed, the former asbestos production site will actually become viable for development

candidates.source_title: Oldham to Rochdale Tram Line - Premier Construction News
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Tramservices have resumed on the Oldham-Rochdale line after essential track replacement work was successfully completed, marking a major milestone in this summer’s programme of network improvements. The work, which took place over a planned two-week closure between Victoria and Rochdale town centre, is part of a wider £150m investment to maintain and improve Greater Manchester’s tram network. It will help deliver a smoother, more reliable service for passengers and support the long-term resilience of the network. Engineers worked day and night between Monsall and Newton Heath & Moston to replace 1.2km of track, improve drainage, renew foundations and correct the alignment and level of the track. It was a big and complex job, using around 290 new concrete sleepers, 2,000 tonnes of gravel and replacing more than 5,000 tonnes of ballast. As a result, sections of the route that previously required speed restrictions can now return to normal operation – up to 50mph on some sections – helping to improve journey times for customers. Ian Davies, TfGM’s Network Director for Metrolink, said: “This was a large and complex piece of engineering, that will make a real difference to the reliability and long-term condition of the network. “It’s the first major milestone of a wider programme of improvements we’re delivering across our tram network this summer to keep it safe, resilient and fit for the future. “We know closing a line is disruptive, and we’re very grateful for everyone continuing to bear with us while this essential work is completed.” Further improvement work will take place at other locations across the Bee Network over the coming months. The most significant being at Trafford Bar and Deansgate-Castlefield. While this work is carried out, there will be no trams on the Eccles, Trafford Centre or Altrincham lines for three weeks from Monday 13 th July to Sunday 2 nd August. Before that, further tram improvement work took place in the city centre . Further work to finish off the job on the Oldham-Rochdale line also took place on Sunday 7 th June and Sunday 12 th July. candidates.source_title: Supermarkets criticised after trolleys end up in canal
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Aldi, Morrisons, and Tesco have been told to ‘get their act together’ by a litter picking group who keep having to haul supermarket trolleys out of a canal. Along a stretch of the Rochdale canal in Failsworth, litter picking group Clean Up Failsworth Canal said they regularly have to drag trolleys out of the water as part of their impressive efforts to clean up the area. The group, which has been running for over 13 years, goes out once a month. Armed with litter pickers and dozens of bags, the team regularly find flytipped rubbish, drinks cans, and nitrous oxide or ‘laughing gas’ cannisters. On September 20, around 22 bags of rubbish had been filled and 26 cannisters were collected while 17 trolleys were fished out of the canal. The trolleys, according to the group, are increasingly becoming a problem. In some areas such as under the bridge to the town’s Tesco car park, the dumped trolleys could even mean boats struggle to get through. Sandra Ball, who represents Failsworth West for Reform UK, said: “Tesco, Aldi, and Morrisons the other end need to get their act together and get it sorted. The trolleys have always been a problem. We have taken 20 out in one session.” She added: “At the end of the day, that cost comes back to us. They have got to pay for [new] trolleys.” Coun Ball has been involved with the group for years. Supported by Oldham council and the Canal and River Trust, she said around 90 people involved in her Failsworth litter busting team. Despite the efforts, she and others feel like it’s a ‘disheartening’ uphill battle, adding: “Within 10 minutes, someone else will have dropped something but if you do not keep on top of it, what would it look like?”

candidates.source_title: Homes powered by Baked Beans could be part of Greater Manchester’s future
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A major plan is being developed that could power thousands of homes with the heat from baked beans, sewage, and data centres. EnergiRaven, a UK-based green energy transition consultancy, is pitching to council bosses to introduce a network of pipes across the region. These would take captured heat from different sources and transport it to people’s homes potentially cutting down on people’s energy bills by up to 38 per cent. Nicknamed the ‘Bee Network for Heat’, the project could link homes across all ten boroughs in Greater Manchester providing heat to thousands. It is based of a publicly-owned model that has been running in Denmark for decades. A map of the network suggests sources of the heat could come from the Baked Beans factory in Wigan, a bread factory near Bolton, various data centres, a number of different industries, wastewater and sewage treatment works, and the Carrington Power Plant. Another map also suggested Kellogg’s plant near Stretford, heat from mine water near Oldham, and Asda’s distribution centre in Rochdale. At an event on September 30, the we heard a data centre in Heywood could heat the equivalent of 50,000 homes. According to EnergiRaven, enough heat could exist across the region to cover 85% of the regions needs and cut down on household bills by 38%. Over 20 years, they say a heat network could save £8.83bn. At the moment, EnergiRaven say heating costs are currently around 8.7p/kWh but this could fall to 5.4p. While gas heating costs in the UK shot up by £1273, it only rose by £271 in Denmark where homes are part of a district heating network. Those behind the scheme say it will protect homes from energy shocks caused by the wars in Iran and Ukraine by tapping into a UK-energy source. Though the scheme will come at a cost, the UK spent £39.3 billion between October 2022 and March 2023 to subsidise energy costs.

Among the DCFC alumni of recent seasons are Jayden Bogle, Jason Knight , Morgan Whittaker, Liam Delap and more. After a handful of appearances for the Rams, he starred on loan in the National League with Gateshead, where he managed nine goals and eight assists in 22 games. However, injury ended his 2024/25 season early having found a place in the DCFC first-team. He then spent last term on loan at Port Vale , where he managed only three goals and three assists in 34 games as they were relegated from League One. A new loan opportunity came knocking in the summer though, with Rochdale bringing Brown in . He has swiftly found a starting role, and after six goalless games to start, the 20-year-old has found form. Brown was on the scoresheet as the Dale won 2-0 against Oldham Athletic , and he followed that up by scoring one and setting up the other in the 2-1 triumph over Fleetwood Town last weekend. His goal was praised by manager Watson post-game , who said this on Brown: “Yes, beautiful goal. That’s two and two for him. So, [the goals] gives him a lot of confidence.”

candidates.source_title: Zambrero opens first Development Agent-supported UK site in Rochdale - L’Express Franchise
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Zambrero has opened a restaurant on Mellor Street in Rochdale, the first UK site to open with support from its Development Agent model. The Mexican quick-service brand opened the unit on 25 September 2026, creating six jobs, and says it is targeting 100 UK sites by 2030 through its franchise programme, putting it among the faster-growing fast food franchises recruiting in the UK . Zambrero entered the UK market in 2021 and now has 18 sites here. Rochdale is its second opening in September, after a restaurant at Brackmills in Northampton earlier in the month. Existing sites span London, Manchester, Birmingham, Reading, Essex, Basingstoke, Northampton and Glasgow. The brand describes itself as a modern Mexican quick-service restaurant franchise. Globally, the brand has more than 350 sites across Australia, Ireland, New Zealand, the United States and the UK. The unit offers dine-in, takeaway and delivery, with seating for 18 customers , and sits near Rochdale town centre and local colleges. The menu covers burritos, bowls, tacos, nachos and quesadillas, with vegetarian, vegan and halal options. The restaurant has created six jobs . It opened on 25 September 2026, and the brand announced it on 1 October. The opening was supported by Zambrero’s Greater Manchester and West Yorkshire Development Agents, Damian Bennett and Dawn Catherall , who gave local guidance and recommendations to the franchise partner. The restaurant has been opened by a multi-brand franchise operator, which has also committed to opening several more Zambrero sites. The operator has not been named, and no number of further sites or details of the Development Agents’ fees or terms have been given. In Zambrero’s UK model, Development Agents are regional contacts who support new franchise partners locally. The description of the role comes from the brand’s own announcement, and the terms are not published. Zambrero is targeting 100 UK sites by 2030 through its franchise programme. With 18 sites trading, that implies about 82 further openings in just over four years, an arithmetic comparison rather than a figure the brand has published, and a rate that depends on recruiting operators rather than on the brand’s own capital, as other networks taking on partners in the UK do.

candidates.source_title: Letter to the editor from a Hopwood Hall volunteer on High Court ruling and restoration hopes
candidates.source_body_excerpt: In regards to the Hopwood Hall Estate Court Case here is my statement as a long standing volunteer. In regards to the Hopwood Hall Estate Court Case here is my statement as a long standing volunteer. I am deeply disappointed and upset by the outcome of the High Court proceedings concerning Hopwood Hall. Having been connected with the Hall for more than two decades, and having actively supported Hopwood DePree and the restoration project since 2013, this is not simply a building or a court case to me. Hopwood Hall has been an important part of my life for many years. My connection with Hopwood Hall actually began around 2003, long before the current restoration project existed. I stumbled across the Hall while walking through the surrounding woods. At that time, as I remember it, there was no fencing immediately around the Hall and I would sometimes sit on the maintained lawn outside. The building was boarded up, but even then it struck me as a hidden gem. There was something about the place that stayed with me. Around 2013, my brother and I became aware that Hopwood DePree had come forward with an interest in saving and restoring his ancestral home. We reached out to him and subsequently met him for the first time at Touchstones in Rochdale, where we went through historical archive material we had found relating to Hopwood Hall. From there, we stayed with the project. My brother and I were involved during its earliest stages and served on the original committee before the official charity was formed. When the project developed and the wider volunteer programme followed, we continued our involvement as volunteers. We were never afraid of getting our hands dirty. We helped with the gardens and grounds, supported restoration activities and assisted at open days, including undertaking security and public-facing duties. Over the years, our voluntary contribution was recognised through a number of awards, something of which we remain extremely proud. For many visitors arriving at Hopwood Hall, my brother and I were among the first people they would meet. We tried to make everyone feel welcome and to represent the project positively. We got to know many people from Middleton and the surrounding community, saw familiar faces returning to open days and had countless conversations with people who cared deeply about the future of the Hall.
